what: The claim that the message 'division by zero' applies 'on 3.14 and newer' is backed by no capture (only 3.15.2 and 3.13.18 ran) and by no source I could find. The 3.14 What's New page doesn't mention it. The 3.13-and-older wording is right: I checked it on 3.12.3 and 3.13.18, including 'integer modulo by zero' for %.
evidence: "division by zero with // or % says division by zero on 3.14 and newer". docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.14.html has no ZeroDivisionError entry. My own runs: 3.12/3.13 print 1//0 -> 'integer division or modulo by zero' and 1%0 -> 'integer modulo by zero'; 3.15.2 prints 'division by zero' for both.
fix: Say "on 3.15 (the version shown)" instead of "3.14 and newer", or cite the CPython changelog entry that made the change.

what: 'There is one safety limit since Python 3.11' isn't backed by a source on the page. The limit was also added to the 3.7–3.10 security releases, and it applies to str→int conversion as well. The capture only shows that the limit exists on 3.13 and 3.15.

fix: Write "in Python 3.11 and newer (and recent security releases of older versions)", and link docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#int-max-str-digits.
